purpose: Meprobamate is used to help relieve anxiety and tension in the short term. It may also be used to help you relax if you are feeling very stressed or nervous. It is usually only recommended for a few weeks at a time.
how_it_works: Meprobamate works by calming down activity in your brain and nervous system. Think of it like turning down the volume on an overactive alarm system in your body. It slows certain signals in the brain that cause feelings of anxiety and tension, helping you feel more relaxed.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or feeling sleepy, dizziness, headache, upset stomach or nausea, and feeling unsteady or clumsy. You may also feel unusually tired when you first start taking it.
warnings: This medication can be habit-forming, so it is important to take it exactly as prescribed and not to take it longer than your doctor recommends. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause serious withdrawal symptoms including seizures. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness dangerously. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 400 mg taken three to four times a day, or 600 mg taken two times a day. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. It is generally used for short periods of time, typically no longer than four months.
